label: For immigrant founders
title: I came to the US with nothing and built companies for immigrants. Now I want to build the next ones with you.
intro: Hey, I'm Siam. Over fifteen years I've guided more than two hundred thousand students abroad, helped immigrants earn millions in US salaries, and run a fund for the ones who made it. Along the way I kept finding problems that deserve a company and don't have one.
These are those openings. Pick one, or bring yours. Tell me what you're great at, building or selling, and I put in the rest, with my three companies and their ecosystem behind you.

pillars.v: Hand-picked from nearly two thousand by the demand behind them and by whether one of my companies already reaches the customer. Each is a one-pager on purpose; the full research comes once we're talking.
Every founder is missing half. Builders lack distribution; sellers lack a product. I map what you don't have and back you with it. Whatever it takes.

Co-founder, equity. Not an agency, not an accelerator. I form the US company, work through the immigration and visa questions with you, and bring the team, the audience and fifteen years of running companies in these markets.

whoIntro: Immigrant founders, solo founders ideally. International students and international founders get preference. I've been one, I've built for hundreds of thousands of them, and I know the constraints. There are two types of founder, and you only need to be one.

icps.name: The Builder
icps.line: A 10× engineer who ships with AI tools at rocket speed and cares how it feels to use.
you: Build end to end (backend, frontend, data, deploy), alone if you have to
Fluent with today's AI coding tools; a working product in weeks, not quarters
Product-minded: you sweat the user experience, not just the architecture
Have shipped something real, even if nobody bought it
we: Distribution: the customers, communities and channels my companies already reach
The first ten conversations, opened for you

icps.name: The Seller
icps.line: Someone who moves people, through a pipeline they've run or an audience that already listens.
you: Can sell anything to anyone, and prove it with a pipeline you've run
Or you make content people actually consume, with a distribution you already own
Live inside a customer community and speak its language
Comfortable charging money from day one
we: Engineering: Algorizin's team builds the product while you sell
The operating playbook from companies that already sell to this audience

ideasTitle: Three stages of an immigrant's life
ideasIntro: Every immigrant goes through three stages. You arrive: you study, adjust and find your footing. You rise: the first job, the career, maybe your own company. Then you thrive: you grow what you built, help others and give back to the community. I've built a company for each stage, and each has ideas waiting for a co-founder. Tap a stage below and pick the ones that fit you.

steps.k: Pick an idea, or bring yours
steps.v: Any one-pager above, or something you've seen that I haven't.
We get to know each other: what you've built or sold, and where you are in the world. Then we brainstorm the idea together, yours or one of mine, and whether it's a company.
Together we work out, plainly, what you're missing and what I'd put in.
Your full commitment for ninety days. Company formed, product launched, first revenue coming in. Then we decide together how big it gets.

closeText: Thirty minutes, no deck needed. Bring what you've built or sold and the idea you can't stop thinking about.
footer: Requests for Co-founders is a project of Siam Hossain and Algorizin, Inc. Ideas are shared as one-pagers on purpose; the research behind each is shared with people we start working with.
